title: Handle SSE disconnection gracefully in lobby UI
Scheduled hider actions: queue veto/randomize before auto-answer deadline
description:
Allow hiders to pre-schedule a powerup action (veto or randomize) in response to a question, so they can take maximum strategic time without risking the auto-answer timer firing before they act.

When a question becomes answerable, the hider has three choices:
1. Answer immediately
2. Wait and answer/play powerup manually before the timer expires
3. Schedule a powerup action — the server holds it and executes it just before the auto-answer would fire

This is important because the hider may want to use the full timer duration strategically (e.g. to move to a better position) but can't risk the auto-answer resolving the question normally.

Key design points:
- New endpoint: POST /questions/{id}/schedule-action with action type (veto/randomize).
- Scheduled action replaces the auto-answer task — if the hider doesn't answer manually before the deadline, the scheduled powerup fires instead of auto-answer.
- Hider can cancel a scheduled action and answer normally instead.
- If hider answers manually before the deadline, the scheduled action is discarded.
- Depends on veto and randomize powerups being implemented first.
close_reason: Scheduled veto implemented via ?scheduled=true on veto endpoint. Auto-answer task checks scheduled_veto flag and vetoes instead of computing answer. Scheduled randomize deferred until randomize powerup (HideAndSeek-fcz) lands.

title: Clean up resolve_station_* reliance on implicit DB ordering

title: Support players leaving mid-game
Early hiding zone declaration + ambiguous overlap resolution
description:
Design doc: `design/hider-station-election.md`

Hiders can voluntarily elect their station during the hiding phase, or the system assigns one at the hiding-to-seeking transition. Ambiguity (0 or 2+ valid candidates) is handled via a dedicated status on the game, with fallback resolution when auto-answer timers fire.

## Key Decisions (from design doc)
- One station per game (hiders travel as a group)
- Election is permanent — no revocation
- All hiders must be within hiding_zone_radius of the elected stop (not just centroid)
- No timing restriction on election
- StationElectionStatus enum: pending | elected | auto_assigned | ambiguous
- Questions blocked while ambiguous; auto-answer fallback resolves first

## Fallback Resolution Cascade
1. All-hiders-in-radius → tightest fit
2. Any-hider-in-radius → shortest min distance
3. Closest (stop, hider) pair

## Endpoints
- GET /nearby-stations?lat=&lng= — stateless, open to all, includes hiding zone polygons
- POST /hider-station — hider-only, permanent election
- GET /hiding-zone?station_id= — open to all, pure geometry query
- GET /hider-station (existing) — extended with station_election_status
close_reason: Cycle 1 implemented: station election, ambiguity handling, fallback cascade, query endpoints

title: Re-model Game object: eliminate untyped dicts
description: Game currently relies heavily on untyped JSON dicts (inventory, timing, etc.) which are error-prone and can produce huge API responses. Replace with properly typed SQLModel fields/tables. Consider splitting into related tables or using typed Pydantic models stored as structured JSON.

title: Opportunistic location updates on API actions
description:
Many API actions are made by players whose current location is known to the client. Rather than relying solely on the dedicated POST /games/{game_id}/location endpoint, we should accept an optional location field on relevant requests and treat it as an implicit location update.

Candidate endpoints:
- POST /games/{game_id}/questions (seeker asking a question — already needs seeker location)
- POST /games/{game_id}/questions/{id}/lock-in (seeker locking in thermometer — uses latest location)
- POST /games/{game_id}/questions/{id}/answer (hider answering — snapshots hider location)

Benefits:
- Reduces location staleness for critical game actions
- Fewer dedicated location report round-trips needed
- More accurate question answers since location is fresh at the moment of action

Implementation:
- Add optional 'coordinates' (GeoJSON Point) + 'timestamp' fields to relevant request schemas
- When present, create a LocationUpdate before processing the main action
- Use the fresh location instead of querying the latest stored one
- Backward compatible: field is optional, existing behavior unchanged if omitted
close_reason: Already implemented — ask endpoints accept seeker location in request body and record it as a LocationUpdate

title: Re-askable questions with escalating cost multiplier
description:
Questions can be asked more than once. Each subsequent ask of the same question costs more — 2x on second ask, 3x on third, etc. This is foundational to the veto and randomize powerups (a vetoed question can be re-asked at multiplied cost, and a randomized original question can be re-asked at its original cost).

Current behavior: asking a question consumes the inventory slot (radar/thermometer) or category usage (matching/measuring) permanently. A consumed slot cannot be reused.

New behavior:
- Slot-based (radar/thermometer): a consumed slot can be re-asked. The cost multiplier determines how many "draws" the hider gets (game mechanic, not server-enforced). The slot's consumed_at is set on first ask; re-asks don't change it.
- Category-based (matching/measuring): a used category can be re-asked. Same multiplier logic.
- Track ask count per (game, question identity) to compute the multiplier. Question identity = slot_index for slot-based, (category, feature_class, question_type) for category-based.
- The "one unanswered question at a time" rule still applies — can't re-ask while the previous instance is pending.
- Vetoed questions reset to re-askable at the current multiplier. Randomized originals reset to re-askable at 1x (original cost).

Open questions:
- Should the multiplier be returned in the ask response so the client can display it?
- How to model ask count — new column on InventorySlot/CategoryUsage, or a separate counter?
- Does the server enforce the cost (e.g. block re-ask if hider hasn't drawn enough cards), or is it trust-based like powerups?
close_reason: Unified InventorySlot model, re-askable slots with ask_count, custom slots, fixed measuring exclusion inversion

title: Fixed radar/thermometer distances per game size with map overrides
description: There's a fixed set of radar and thermometer distances available in every game based on its size (small/medium/large). Game maps should be able to include extras or exclude defaults from this base set. Distances are part of inventory and should be tracked as consumed/available.
close_reason: Implemented DistanceConvention enum, conventions.py module, field renames, conversion boundary in logic.py, code-level default inventory, imperial manual test script. All 143 tests pass.

title: Seeker abandon question: drop current question without an answer
description: Allow seekers to abandon the current answerable question, accepting no answer and no exclusion zone. Useful when a randomize powerup changes the question to something undesirable (e.g. thermometer with unreasonable travel distance). The abandoned question should behave like a vetoed question from the data perspective (no answer, no exclusion, terminal status). May need a new status (e.g. 'abandoned') or reuse 'vetoed'. Seekers can then ask a new question immediately.
close_reason: Implemented in commit 246f97d — POST /questions/{qid}/abandon endpoint, abandon_question logic, validate_abandon_request, tests, CLAUDE.md updated

title: Audit models for dangerous high-cardinality relationship potentials
description: Review all SQLAlchemy relationship() declarations across models/ for relationships that could load unbounded result sets (e.g., Game.questions, Game.players, LocationUpdate backrefs). Identify which should use lazy='dynamic' or be accessed only via explicit queries. Check for N+1 patterns in router/logic code that iterate over high-cardinality relationships.

title: POST /location should return 204 instead of visible players
description: The POST /location endpoint currently returns LocationReportResponse with a 'players' list (visible seekers). This couples a write (report my position) with a read (who can I see) and the response is useless in most cases (empty in 1v1 games). The endpoint should just return 204 No Content on success. If the client needs visible player positions, that should be a separate GET endpoint or come through the game state. Remove LocationReportResponse, VisiblePlayer, VisiblePlayerData, and get_visible_players — they're only used by this endpoint.

title: Refactor game queries into action-oriented functions
description: The single update_game_status and monolithic GET /games/{id} are becoming cumbersome as more fields are added (hider_station_id, hiding_zone_radius_override, etc). Break game mutations into specific action functions (e.g., set_hider_station, set_hiding_zone_override) and consider splitting the game read into focused queries rather than always loading the full game with all relationships.
close_reason: Game state endpoint split (58932d2) replaced the monolithic GET /games/{id} with role-gated focused endpoints. Game mutations already use action-oriented functions (set_hider_station, etc). Remaining refactoring can be done as needed.

title: Migrate in-game push events to broadcast emit()
description: Existing in-game push-only events (phase_changed, question_asked, question_answered, etc.) should be migrated to use broadcast.emit() for consistency. Currently they call send_push.delay() directly from routers. This is a follow-up to Cycle 3 (SSE + Redis pub/sub for lobby). In-game SSE channel: game:{id}:game:events (separate lifecycle, auth, event types from lobby).

title: Endgame Cycle 3: Seeker proximity notifications
slot_index refers to remaining slots instead of original template positions
description:
When asking a radar/thermometer question, slot_index indexes into the list of *unconsumed* slots rather than the original inventory template. After consuming slot 1 (0.5 mi), sending slot_index=4 expecting the 5 mi slot actually selects 10 mi because the array shifted.

This is confusing and error-prone for clients — they'd need to track which slots have been consumed and recompute indices. The slot_index should refer to the original template position (stable across the game), and the server should validate that the slot hasn't already been consumed.

Discovered during manual testing: asked slot_index=4 expecting 5 mi radar, got 10 mi instead.
close_reason: Closed

title: Add district borders to Seattle GameMap seed script
description: The seed_seattle_map.py script creates the Seattle GameMap with boundary and 5 KCC district polygons, but district borders (the shared edges between adjacent districts) aren't included. These would be useful for rendering district boundaries on the client map. Determine the right representation (LineString edges? derived from district polygons?) and add them to the seed data.
close_reason: District borders computed from shapely intersection, stored as MapFeature rows with admin_division_border category

title: send_push task fails with DetachedInstanceError on DeviceToken
description: The send_push Celery task loads DeviceToken objects but then accesses their attributes after the session scope closes, causing DetachedInstanceError. Retries exhaust and the push is lost. Seen in Docker testing with real Redis + Celery worker. The task in tasks/push.py calls push.py:send_to_tokens which accesses token attributes outside the session. Fix: ensure token values are extracted into plain strings before closing the session.
close_reason: Closed

title: Randomize powerup: hider forces a random replacement question
description:
Hider plays a randomize powerup in response to any answerable question. Instead of answering, the server:
1. Notifies seekers that a randomize was played.
2. Seekers must choose (randomly — dice/RNG) a different unasked question from the same category. For slot-based questions (radar/thermometer), this means a different slot. For category-based (matching/measuring), this means a different category.
3. The randomly chosen replacement question is automatically asked, and the hider answers it normally.
4. The original question is NOT considered asked — it can be re-asked later at its original cost.

Key design points:
- Trust-based: no card/hand tracking. Hider assumed to have the powerup.
- The replacement must be from the same category but different parameters (e.g. 10mi radar → 50mi radar).
- If the replacement resolves to a null answer, that's valid (tough luck).
- The original slot/category is restored (not consumed).
- Auto-answer timer on the original question is revoked; a new timer starts on the replacement.
- Push flow: hider plays randomize → push to seekers → seekers pick random replacement → replacement is asked → hider answers.

Open questions:
- Should the server enforce randomness of the replacement, or trust the seekers to pick randomly?
- How to handle the intermediate state between randomize played and replacement selected?
- What if there are no other unasked questions in the same category?

title: Endgame Cycle 2: Hiding station codification

title: Migrate mobile app from SwiftUI to React Native
close_reason: Scaffolded Expo React Native app in mobile/, deleted ios/. Includes expo-router, react-native-maps, type-safe API client, strict linting (type-aware ESLint + prettier), and pre-commit hooks.

title: Discipline test suite: mock DB in unit tests, reserve real DB for query/integration tests
description:
Unit tests currently import internal functions (e.g., `_buffer` from exclusion.py) and mix DB access into logic tests. This makes tests brittle and couples them to implementation details.

**Goals:**
- **Unit tests** (logic/, exclusion, conventions, geo): mock DB access (`get_session`, `register`, query functions). Test business logic in isolation with plain objects/fixtures.
- **Query tests**: use real DB (testcontainers PostGIS) to test query functions against actual SQL.
- **Integration tests** (via TestClient): use real DB, test full request→response flows through the router stack.
- Stop importing private/internal functions (e.g., `_buffer`) — test through public interfaces instead.
- Consider splitting test files to reflect the unit/query/integration boundary (e.g., `test_exclusion_unit.py` vs `test_exclusion_integration.py`, or subdirectories).

**Why:**
- Faster unit tests (no DB overhead for pure logic)
- Tests that break only when behavior changes, not when internals are refactored
- Clearer test boundaries matching the layered architecture (routers → logic → queries)

title: Replace timing JSON blob with real columns
description: Game.timing is an unstructured sa.JSON dict with string-key access and magic defaults (hiding_time_min=30, location_question_delay_min=5). Replace with proper typed columns on both Game and GameMap. Consumers should read real fields instead of .get() with fallback strings.
close_reason: Replaced timing JSON blob with typed columns on Game, added map-level defaults on GameMap

title: Player authentication: server-generated secrets to prevent client_id spoofing
close_reason: All 5 cycles complete: model changes, endpoint/dependency updates, test updates, mobile auth flow, documentation. 224 tests pass, manual E2E verified on iOS simulator.

title: Veto powerup: hider refuses to answer a question
description:
Hider plays a veto powerup in response to any answerable question. The question goes unanswered — seekers are informed the hider used a veto but get no answer. The question is NOT considered consumed: seekers can re-ask the same question, but at multiplied cost (2x on second ask, 3x on third, etc.).

Key design points:
- Trust-based: no card/hand tracking on server. Hider is assumed to have the powerup.
- Veto replaces the answer action — hider hits a veto endpoint instead of the answer endpoint.
- Auto-answer timer must be revoked when veto is played (same as normal answer).
- Question status should reflect that it was vetoed (new status? or answered with a special answer value?).
- Push notification to seekers: "The hider used a veto! No answer this time."
- The re-ask cost multiplier mechanic (questions can be asked more than once, cost doubles each time) is a prerequisite — may need its own implementation work.

Open questions:
- Should vetoed questions have a distinct status (e.g. `vetoed`) or use `answered` with `answer=null`?
- How to track ask count per question identity for cost multiplier?
close_reason: Implemented veto endpoint, vetoed status, push event, tests, and docs

title: Support metric and imperial distance conventions
description: Games support both metric (meters/km) and imperial (miles) conventions. Radar/thermometer distance inventory differs between conventions (not a perfect conversion — e.g., 3km vs 2mi). The API surface must communicate distances in the selected convention so clients don't handle conversion/presentation.
close_reason: Implemented DistanceConvention enum, conventions.py module, field renames, conversion boundary in logic.py, code-level default inventory, imperial manual test script. All 143 tests pass.

title: Audit GET /games/{id} and GET /maps/{id} response sizes
description:
Both endpoints return everything in a single response and will grow with the data:

- GET /games/{id}: full inventory template (13 slots), all players, timing, timestamps. The inventory is static after game creation — no reason to re-send it every poll. Players rarely change after lobby.
- GET /maps/{id}: full boundary polygon (47+ pts), all district polygons (up to 144 pts each, 5 districts = ~450 pts), district_classes, full default_inventory. The boundary and districts are large geometry payloads that never change.

Consider:
1. Splitting static vs dynamic data (e.g., map geometry fetched once, game status polled frequently)
2. ETag/conditional GET for map data
3. Separate endpoints for heavy sub-resources (boundary, districts, inventory template)
4. Pagination or lazy loading for districts if maps grow to many districts

Not urgent for a single Seattle map and small games, but will matter if we add more maps or support larger player counts.
close_reason: Not a real concern — these endpoints are called infrequently

title: Expand hiding zone powerup: increase hiding zone radius mid-game
description:
Hider plays a powerup to expand the hiding zone radius during the seeking phase. This makes it harder for seekers to narrow down the hider's location, since the candidate station pool grows and exclusion coverage becomes less effective relative to the larger zone.

Key design points:
- Trust-based: no card/hand tracking. Hider assumed to have the powerup.
- The hiding zone radius is currently implicit (derived from the hider's station and map geometry). This powerup would need an explicit radius override or multiplier on the game.
- Expansion should be a fixed increment or multiplier (e.g. +50%, or +X convention units). TBD what feels balanced.
- Can likely be played at any time during seeking, not just in response to a question.
- Affects candidate stations and endgame exclusion calculations — both use the hiding zone.
- Push notification to all players: "The hider has expanded the hiding zone!"
- Should there be a limit on how many times this can be played? (Probably trust-based — hider only has so many cards.)

Open questions:
- Fixed increment vs percentage multiplier for the expansion?
- Can it be stacked (played multiple times)?
- New endpoint: POST /games/{id}/expand-hiding-zone, or a generic powerup endpoint?
- How to store the override — new column on Game (e.g. hiding_zone_radius_multiplier)?
- Does the hider need to have reached seeking phase, or can they play it during hiding?

title: Add default_timing to GameMap with optional per-game override
description: GameMap should have an optional default_timing that provides timing defaults for games created on that map. Game.timing should override map defaults (game values take precedence, fall back to map). Currently timing={} is hardcoded in the create endpoint with a TODO.
close_reason: Replaced timing JSON blob with typed columns on Game, added map-level defaults on GameMap

title: Category availability via feature inclusion, not exclusion
description: Rather than explicit exclusions on game maps, determine available categories/questions based on what features are actually defined. Later support opt-in for Google Places API categories. Remove excluded_categories from GameMap and derive availability from GameMapFeature presence.
close_reason: Removed excluded_categories from GameMap. Category availability is now purely inclusion-based: derived from GameMapFeature records on the map, filtered by question type support and already-used inventory.

title: Remove dead feature_classes field from GameMap
close_reason: Removed dead feature_classes field from GameMap

title: Design and implement exclusion zones
description: When questions are answered, they create exclusion zones on the map that narrow down the hider's possible location. Need to design the geometry computation (based on question type and answer) and store/serve these zones. Game maps can be multi-polygons, so exclusion zones can also be multi-polygons.
close_reason: Implemented exclusion zone computation for all four question types (radar, thermometer, matching, measuring) with cumulative total_exclusion tracking. Answer functions in logic.py now generate and persist exclusion geometry.

title: Implement tentacles question type
Redesign question inventory model
description: Current inventory model is awkward — slot-based for radar/thermometer, category-key lists for matching/measuring, all stuffed in a JSON dict on Game. Redesign to be cleaner: possibly a separate table or well-typed model. Should integrate with radar/thermometer distance sets and matching/measuring category tracking.
close_reason: Implemented: relational InventorySlot/CategoryUsage tables replace game.inventory JSON; per-type param tables (RadarParams, ThermometerParams, FeatureQuestionParams) replace question.parameters JSON; per-type ask endpoints

title: Clean up response schemas: eliminate noise nulls and tighten write responses
description:
Several API responses return fields that are always null/meaningless in context:

1. **QuestionDetailResponse (write endpoints)**: When returned from ask/answer POSTs, fields like seeker_location_end, hider_location, answered_at, answer are all null on ask, and seeker_location_end is null for non-thermometer types always. Consider splitting into AskResponse (just id + status + params) vs FullDetailResponse, or at minimum exclude_none in serialization.

2. **answerable_at on radar questions**: Always ~0.1ms after asked_at (meaningless). This field only matters for thermometers. Could omit for non-thermometer types.

3. **GameResponse nulls in early states**: hiding_started_at and seeking_started_at are null in lobby/hiding. join_code persists into seeking (should be nulled at transition — it already is in the DB but only when the game ends, not at seeking start).

These are cosmetic but they make the API feel unpolished and force the client to handle many null cases that conceptually can't happen.
close_reason: Implemented: AskQuestionResponse for ask endpoints, removed answerable_at from summary/detail, join_code cleared at hiding start

title: GameStatus: move status checks to instance methods on enum
close_reason: Added is_active property to GameStatus enum, replaced inline {hiding, seeking} set checks

title: Support question slicing on long-game exclusions and candidate stations
description: The endgame-exclusions endpoint supports after_question for slicing the question set. The long-game equivalents (GET /exclusions and GET /candidate-stations) have no such support — they always use the full set of answered questions. Add an optional after_question (or similar) param to both endpoints so the client can compute exclusion zones and candidate stations from a subset of questions (e.g., 'show me exclusions from question 3 onward'). This enables progressive replay and what-if analysis during seeking.

title: Transit data: include all stops, exclude per-game
description: Transit datasets should include ALL stops in the game area. Per-game exclusions determine which stops/lines the hider cannot hide at. Some question types don't distinguish between used and unused stops — the data model needs to support this.
close_reason: Moved excluded_stop_ids and excluded_route_ids from GameMap to Game. Exclusions are now per-game, set at creation time via CreateGameRequest.

title: Avoid redundant game DB fetch: use question.game relationship instead of dependency-injected game
description: Several endpoints (e.g. answer, veto, abandon, lock-in) fetch a Game via dependency injection (get_game from the URL path) AND also query a Question that already has a game relationship. We could skip the separate game fetch and instead use question.game after looking up the question. This would reduce redundant DB queries and simplify the dependency chain. Audit all endpoints that take both a game_id path param and a question_id — candidates include answer, veto, abandon, lock-in, and question detail.

title: Run test suite against real PostgreSQL/PostGIS containers
description: Currently all tests run against in-memory SQLite+SpatiaLite. Some spatial queries (ST_Buffer on Geography, ST_DWithin, etc.) are PostGIS-only and are skipped. Add a pytest configuration or CI step that runs the full test suite against a real PostgreSQL+PostGIS container (e.g., via docker compose or testcontainers-python). This catches PostGIS-specific behavior differences, SQL dialect quirks, and ensures the 'ss' (skipped) tests actually work.
close_reason: Implemented in f2c4180: testcontainers spins up PostGIS container for all tests, SQLite removed entirely
